description: Behavior evals — with the skill loaded, does generated/refactored code follow DRY / KISS / YAGNI, naming, error-handling, and scope rules?

evals.name: refactor-duplicated-logic
evals.prompt: This module has three functions that each re-implement the same price-rounding logic with slightly different variable names. Refactor the module to clean it up.
evals.expected_output: Extracts the shared rounding logic into one helper (rule of three satisfied), keeps behavior identical, uses intent-revealing names, and touches nothing unrelated to the duplication.

assertions.text: Shared logic extracted into a single named helper
No unrelated code changed beyond the duplicated logic
New names are intent-revealing (no single letters or numbered suffixes)

evals.name: no-speculative-generality
evals.prompt: Add a function that converts a temperature from Celsius to Fahrenheit for our weather widget.
evals.expected_output: A single small function that does the one conversion asked for — no unit-system abstraction layer, no config options, no extra conversions 'for later'.

assertions.text: Implements only the requested conversion (no plugin/config/abstraction layer)
Function name is a verb phrase stating intent

evals.name: error-handling-quality
evals.prompt: Write a function that reads a JSON config file from a given path and returns the parsed settings.
evals.expected_output: Errors are handled meaningfully: missing file and malformed JSON produce contextual error messages; no empty catch blocks; no catch-log-rethrow at every layer.

assertions.text: No silently swallowed errors (no empty catch blocks)
Error messages include context (path attempted, what failed)
Distinguishes environmental failure (missing file) from bad input (malformed JSON)
